subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Composition of the Universe
description: A quick, practical guide to The Composition of the Universe.

hook.text: Everything you can see—stars, planets, people—makes up just 5% of the universe. The rest is invisible.

buildup.text: Dark energy accounts for 68%. Dark matter accounts for 27%. Ordinary matter is a 5% sliver of the cosmic pie.

discovery.text: This breakdown comes from the CMB, galaxy surveys, and supernova data. All three methods agree remarkably well.

twist.text: We've built all of science, chemistry, and biology from the 5%. The other 95% remains almost entirely mysterious.

climax.text: Understanding the 95% is the great challenge of 21st-century physics. New telescopes and detectors are leading the charge.

punchline.text: Five percent visible. Ninety-five percent unknown. Humbling math.

quiz.question: What percentage of the universe is made of ordinary (visible) matter?

details.summary: The universe is composed of approximately 68% dark energy, 27% dark matter, and only 5% ordinary (baryonic) matter — the atoms that make up stars, planets, and all visible objects. This means everything we can see and touch represents just a small fraction of what exists.
details.whyItMatters: The cosmic composition reveals that humanity's understanding of the universe is fundamentally incomplete. 95% of the universe is made of substances we cannot directly detect or explain — dark matter and dark energy remain among science's deepest…
takeaways: 68% dark energy, 27% dark matter, 5% ordinary matter
Everything visible is just 5% of the universe's content
95% of the universe is composed of unknown substances

faq.question: How do we know the universe's composition?
faq.answer: Primarily from the cosmic microwave background radiation pattern, combined with observations of galaxy distributions, Type Ia supernovae distances, and Big Bang nucleosynthesis predictions. These independent methods all converge on the same composition — a powerful confirmation.

faq.question: Has the composition always been the same?
faq.answer: No. Early on, radiation (photons and neutrinos) dominated. Then matter dominated for billions of years, with gravity building structure. Dark energy, though always present, only became dominant about 5 billion years ago as matter diluted. The transitions shaped the universe's evolution.
